0.250528.0702, the only published version. The paper cites the dandiset without a version, so the
latest published version is pinned (see `dandi_io.py`). The mouse Neuropixels data used for
figs37a are in [DANDI:001326](https://dandiarchive.org/dandiset/001326/0.250528.1957), version
0.250528.1957, its only published version.

**What this notebook reads.** For the 7 included iEEG participants (SD168, SD172, SD181, SD185,
SD186, SD211, SD245), the per-session files `sub-SD*/sub-SD*_ses-puff<Session>_ecephys.nwb`
(LFP at 200 Hz, 20 min around the eyepuff assay, an electrode table with region labels, and 20 DC
channels, one of which carries the puff TTL) and the behaviour files
`sub-SD*/sub-SD*_ses-puff_behavior.nwb` (trials used, puff frames of the video, per-trial eye
closure). For figs37a, the 13 Neuropixels sessions of DANDI:001326, processed with the entry's
`mouse_npx.py`.

**Outside input.** The paper's code record
[Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.14920570](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14920570)
(`kauvar-richman-liu-2025_zenodo.zip`, md5 bd1fb567121aaf0291337783df57bcfc, git commit b873ca5)
is fetched at run time and its md5 checked. Two things are read from it: the list of bad channels
per participant (`ketman/analyze/utils.py`, `bad_ch`; the dataset does not mark bad channels), a
method detail shown as one reading against the dataset-only channel set; and the Yeo7 network label
of each bipolar channel (`anat/pts_ch_labels.pkl`), which the dataset lacks and which figs35 needs
(`data: with_labels`, tested by the link claim `ieeg-channel-atlas-link`). The analysis follows the
code (`human_ieeg/scripts/analyze_airpuff_ieeg_cd.py`, `ketman/analyze/trace_utils.py`,
`cd_utils.py`, `for_reference/analyze_airpuff_ieeg_top_cd_network.py`), reimplemented in
`ieeg_cd.py`, whose docstring says where each parameter comes from.

Random numbers: the random-time null of the clock check uses seed 0 per participant, the Yeo7
shuffle uses seed 1.

| Claim | Data | Status |
|---|---|---|
| fig6c-human-persistent-activity-reduced | dataset | tested |
| fig6e-human-fast-activity-unchanged | dataset | tested |
| figs37c-persistent-reduction-across-bands | dataset | tested |
| figs37b-fast-unchanged-across-bands | dataset | tested |
| fig6g-human-timescale-shorter | dataset | tested |
| fig6i-human-coupling-reduced | dataset | tested |
| figs38a-baseline-coupling-not-different | dataset | tested |
| figs38b-ketamine-coupling-loss-larger-at-persistent-sites | dataset | tested |
| figs38h-prepuff-coupling-predicts-persistence | dataset | tested |
| ieeg-channel-atlas-link (link) | with labels | tested |
| figs35-persistent-dimension-distributed | with labels | tested |
| figs37a-beta-most-similar-to-mouse | with inputs | tested |
""")

code(r"""
import os, time, warnings
os.environ.setdefault("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "1")
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import scipy.stats as st
import yaml
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests

import dandi_io
import ieeg_cd as ic

pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 30)
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 200)
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=RuntimeWarning)

T0 = time.time()
with open("../../claims/001347/10.1126-science.adt3971.yaml") as f:
    CLAIMS = {c["id"]: c for c in yaml.safe_load(f)["claims"]}

def expected(cid):
    # Expected values of a claim, read from the claims file for comparison only.
    return [(e["quantity"], e["value"], e.get("tolerance")) for e in CLAIMS[cid].get("expected", [])]

ZF = ic.fetch_code_zip()
BAD = ic.code_bad_channels(ZF)
LABELS = ic.code_channel_labels(ZF)
print("code record fetched, md5 checked; bad-channel lists for",
      sum(pt in BAD for pt in ic.PARTICIPANTS), "of 7 participants")
""")

md(r"""
## Data check

Every participant's sessions are listed from the archive, and one file's electrode table is shown
in full. The processing cell then streams the 22 LFP files used (three per participant, plus
SD245's Preinfusion file, which the code does not use for the coding dimension; see below) and
reduces each to what the claims need. It runs the participants in three parallel processes and
takes about 8 to 10 minutes.
""")

code(r"""
assets = dandi_io.list_assets()
rows = []
for pt in ic.PARTICIPANTS:
    ses = sorted(p.split("_ses-puff")[1].split("_")[0] for p in assets
                 if p.startswith(f"sub-{pt}/") and p.endswith("_ecephys.nwb"))
    beh_file = f"sub-{pt}/sub-{pt}_ses-puff_behavior.nwb" in assets
    rows.append(dict(participant=pt, ecephys_sessions=", ".join(ses), behaviour_file=beh_file,
                     preinfusion_file_code=ic.PRE_SESSION_CODE[pt]))
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_string(index=False))

f = dandi_io.open_h5("sub-SD181/sub-SD181_ses-puffPreinfusion_ecephys.nwb")
e = f["general/extracellular_ephys/electrodes"]
print("\nelectrode table columns:", list(e.attrs["colnames"]))
for col in e.attrs["colnames"]:
    if col == "group":
        continue
    v = e[col][:]
    print(f"  {col}: {len(v)} rows, first values {v[:3]}" +
          (f", NaN fraction {np.isnan(v).mean():.2f}" if v.dtype.kind == "f" else ""))
ts = f["processing/ecephys/LFP/v_trace"]
print("LFP:", ts["data"].shape, "unit attribute:", ts["data"].attrs["unit"],
      "| comments:", ts.attrs["comments"], "| rate:", ts["starting_time"].attrs["rate"])
print("DC channels:", [x.decode() for x in f["acquisition/dc_channels/channel_name"][:]])
""", "sanity")

code(r"""
t = time.time()
RES, ALT, BEH = ic.run_all(BAD, max_workers=3)
EX = ic.extra_session(RES["SD245"], "Preinfusion")
print(f"processed in {time.time() - t:.0f} s")
""")

code(r"""
rows = []
for pt in ic.PARTICIPANTS:
    r, b = RES[pt], BEH[pt]
    wt = b["which_trials"]
    for c in ic.CONDITIONS:
        s = r["sessions"][c]
        bkey = ic.BEHAVIOUR_PRE[r["pre_ses"]] if c == "preinfusion" else c
        vid = b["events"][bkey]
        n = min(len(vid), len(s["puffs"]))
        d = np.diff(s["puffs"][:n]) - np.diff(vid[:n])
        rows.append(dict(pt=pt, cond=c, file=s["file_session"], mono=s["n_mono"], bipolar=s["n_pairs"],
                         ttl_puffs=len(s["puffs"]), first_puff_sample=s["puffs"][0],
                         video_puffs=len(vid), max_interval_diff_samples=int(np.abs(d).max()),
                         trials_used=len(wt), max_trial_index=int(wt.max()),
                         raw_p1=round(s["raw_range"][0]), raw_p99=round(s["raw_range"][1]),
                         dc2_name=s["dc_name"]))
chk = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(chk.to_string(index=False))
print("\ntrials used per participant:", {pt: len(BEH[pt]["which_trials"]) for pt in ic.PARTICIPANTS},
      "total", sum(len(BEH[pt]["which_trials"]) for pt in ic.PARTICIPANTS))

rows = []
for pt in ic.PARTICIPANTS:
    pr, m = RES[pt]["pairs"], RES[pt]["masks"]
    labels = set(pr["a"]) | set(pr["b"])
    rows.append(dict(pt=pt, bipolar_pairs=len(pr), out_of_brain_or_excluded=int(pr["excluded"].sum()),
                     white_matter=int(pr["wm"].sum()),
                     kept_wm_excl=int(m[(True, "none")].sum()), kept_wm_excl_codebad=int(m[(True, "code")].sum()),
                     kept_all=int(m[(False, "none")].sum()), kept_all_codebad=int(m[(False, "code")].sum()),
                     code_bad_listed=len(BAD[pt]), code_bad_found_in_labels=sum(x in labels for x in BAD[pt])))
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_string(index=False))
""", "sanity")

code(r"""
# Clock check: the band-power change after the puff (beta, mean over 0.05 to 1.5 s minus 0.5 s
# before, averaged over trials, absolute value averaged over channels), at the TTL puff times,
# at 20 sets of 40 random times in the 10 min before the assay, and at the TTL times shifted by
# -2.5 s and +2.5 s.
rows = []
for pt in ic.PARTICIPANTS:
    c = RES[pt]["clock"]
    rows.append(dict(pt=pt, true=c["true"], random_mean=c["null"].mean(), random_max=c["null"].max(),
                     shift_minus2p5=c["shift"][0], shift_plus2p5=c["shift"][1],
                     true_over_random_max=c["true"] / c["null"].max()))
clock = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(clock.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print("participants whose true value exceeds every random set:", int((clock.true > clock.random_max).sum()), "of 7")
""", "sanity")

md(r"""
Checks of the metadata against the data:

- Session files. SD168 and SD172 have no Preinfusion file; their pre-infusion eyepuff session is
  the Baseline file, recorded the day before (`ketman/DATASETS.py`). The code takes the Baseline
  file as "preinfusion" for these two. For SD245 the code lists both Baseline and Preinfusion and
  renames 'baseline' to 'preinfusion' after loading, which replaces the Preinfusion data by the
  Baseline data in the coding-dimension path (`load_and_organize_raw_traces`,
  `load_patients_erp`), while the timescale path (`load_raw_traces_and_merge_to_anat`) keeps the
  Preinfusion file. SD245's behaviour file holds only 'baseline' eye-closure events. Both SD245
  files are run here as readings.
- Puff times. The TTL is on DC channel index 2, named 'CCEP' in the file, not on a channel named
  for the TTL. 40 onsets are found in every preinfusion session, with the first at sample about
  120000, the middle of the 20-min epoch, as the epoch description ("10 min pre and post puff
  start") says. Their intervals match the puff frames of the 200-Hz video within the number of
  samples printed above, and the puff-locked beta-power change at the TTL times is larger than at
  every random set of times and at the shifted times for the participants counted above. The
  puff times are consistent with sharing the LFP clock.
- Trials. The trials used (`which_trials` of the behaviour files) total 214 across participants,
  the number Table S3 gives for fig. S38H.
- Units. The LFP's unit attribute is 'volts', but the values are of order 100 to 1000 and the
  series comment and device description give a 'scale_to_microvolts' factor (0.39 or 0.098), so
  the stored values are digitiser units. All analyses here are z-scored, so the scale does not
  matter. The x, y, z columns of the electrode table are all NaN.
- Channels. The dataset gives a region label per contact, including 'WM', 'OUT OF BRAIN',
  'EXCLUDE' and 'EXCLUDE AREA', but no bad-channel flag and no Yeo7 network label.
""")

# ---- fig6c
md(r"""
## fig6c-human-persistent-activity-reduced

> In humans, eyepuff-evoked activity along the persistent (beta band power) dimension falls during
> ketamine (1.36 to 0.41) and partly recovers after infusion (0.72).

Criterion: H-CD with the persistent window, beta band; reproduced when, under a combination of
readings of Open C and Open D, both corrected p < 0.05 in the stated direction and the three means
are within tolerance. The table shows every combination of Open C (Methods or code z-scoring),
Open D (white matter excluded or kept), the bad-channel list (none, or the code's), the code's
per-trial baseline subtraction (with or without) and SD245's preinfusion file (Baseline as in the
code, or Preinfusion).
""")
code(r"""
print("expected:", expected("fig6c-human-persistent-activity-reduced"))
T6C = ic.readings_table(RES, ALT, "beta", "persistent")
lo = [v - t for _, v, t in expected("fig6c-human-persistent-activity-reduced")]
hi = [v + t for _, v, t in expected("fig6c-human-persistent-activity-reduced")]
T6C["means_in_tol"] = [(lo[0] <= a <= hi[0]) and (lo[1] <= b <= hi[1]) and (lo[2] <= c <= hi[2])
                       for a, b, c in zip(T6C.pre, T6C.ket, T6C.post)]
T6C["tests_hold"] = ((T6C.pcorr_pre_ket < 0.05) & (T6C.t_pre_ket > 0) &
                     (T6C.pcorr_post_ket < 0.05) & (T6C.t_post_ket > 0))
cols = ["open_c", "wm_excluded", "bad_list", "trial_baseline", "sd245_pre", "pre", "ket", "post",
        "t_pre_ket", "pcorr_pre_ket", "t_post_ket", "pcorr_post_ket", "tests_hold", "means_in_tol"]
print(T6C[cols].round(3).to_string())
print("\nreadings with tests holding:", int(T6C.tests_hold.sum()), "of", len(T6C),
      "| tests and means:", int((T6C.tests_hold & T6C.means_in_tol).sum()))
for key, g in T6C.groupby(["open_c", "bad_list"]):
    print(key, "tests hold", int(g.tests_hold.sum()), "of", len(g), "| tests and means", int((g.tests_hold & g.means_in_tol).sum()))
""", "claim:fig6c-human-persistent-activity-reduced")
code(r"""
# Per participant, the code's readings (Open C code, white matter excluded, code bad list,
# per-trial baseline, SD245 Baseline file), and with the dataset-only channel set.
for bad in ("code", "none"):
    v = ic.cd_summary(RES, ALT, "beta", "persistent", True, bad, True, "code")
    df = pd.DataFrame(v, index=ic.PARTICIPANTS)
    print(f"bad list = {bad}"); print(df.round(3).to_string())
    print("ketamine below preinfusion in", int((df.infusion < df.preinfusion).sum()), "of 7;",
          "postinfusion above ketamine in", int((df.postinfusion > df.infusion).sum()), "of 7")
tr = {c: ic.cd_summary(RES, ALT, "beta", "persistent", True, "code", True, "code", traces=True)[c] for c in ic.CONDITIONS}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4, 2.6))
for c, col in zip(ic.CONDITIONS, ["k", "m", "c"]):
    m, s = tr[c].mean(0), st.sem(tr[c], axis=0)
    ax.plot(ic.TT - 0.05, m, col, label=c); ax.fill_between(ic.TT - 0.05, m - s, m + s, color=col, alpha=0.2)
ax.set_xlim(-1, 2); ax.set_xlabel("time from puff (s, code axis)"); ax.set_ylabel("projection (z)"); ax.legend(fontsize=7)
print("plotted range of the mean traces:", round(min(tr[c].mean(0).min() for c in tr), 2), "to", round(max(tr[c].mean(0).max() for c in tr), 2))
plt.show()
""", "claim:fig6c-human-persistent-activity-reduced")
md(r"""
**Result: reproduced under the code's z-scoring (Open C reading b), the paper's numbers recovered.**
With the code's readings (white matter excluded, the code's bad-channel list, SD245 Baseline file)
the means are 1.363, 0.411 and 0.724, with t = 5.876 (corrected p = 0.002) for preinfusion against
ketamine and t = 3.172 (corrected p = 0.019) for postinfusion against ketamine; the paper gives
1.36, 0.41, 0.72, t = 5.887 and 3.171. With white matter kept (Open D b) the three means are also
within tolerance. Without the code's bad-channel list the tests hold in every Open C (b) reading,
and the means are within tolerance with white matter kept (1.391, 0.472, 0.828) but not with it
excluded (ketamine 0.482, just above 0.48). Under the Methods z-scoring (Open C a) the preinfusion
mean is about 1.6 in every reading, outside tolerance, while the preinfusion test holds in all
readings. Ketamine is below preinfusion in all 7 participants.
""")

md(r"""
## fig6e-human-fast-activity-unchanged

Criterion: a claim of absence judged on the paper's test; reproduced when both corrected p >= 0.05.
""")

T6E = ic.readings_table(RES, ALT, "beta", "fast")
T6E["both_ns"] = (T6E.pcorr_pre_ket >= 0.05) & (T6E.pcorr_post_ket >= 0.05)
from ieeg_cd import st as _st
T6E["cohen_dz_pre_ket"] = np.nan

        "t_pre_ket", "pcorr_pre_ket", "t_post_ket", "pcorr_post_ket", "both_ns"]
print(T6E[cols].round(3).to_string())
for key, g in T6E.groupby(["open_c", "bad_list"]):

print(f"pre - ket mean {d.mean():.3f}, Cohen dz {d.mean() / d.std(ddof=1):.2f}, 95% CI of the mean difference "
      f"{d.mean() - st.t.ppf(0.975, 6) * st.sem(d):.3f} to {d.mean() + st.t.ppf(0.975, 6) * st.sem(d):.3f}")
""", "claim:fig6e-human-fast-activity-unchanged")
md(r"""
**Result: reproduced, resting on the code's z-scoring (Open C reading b) where the bad-channel list
is the code's.** Under the code's readings the means are 4.120, 4.006 and 3.866 with t = 0.433
(corrected p = 0.680) for preinfusion against ketamine, matching the paper's 4.12, 4.00, 3.86 and
t = 0.432. Without the code's bad-channel list no reading gives a corrected p below 0.05. With the
code's list and the Methods z-scoring (Open C a), postinfusion against ketamine gives corrected

md(r"""
## figs37c-persistent-reduction-across-bands

> The ketamine reduction of the persistent projection holds in every band except broadband LFP, and
> recovers significantly after infusion in delta and beta.

Criterion: H-CD with the persistent window in each band, under the readings that reproduce fig6c;
reproduced when pre against ketamine is significant in each filtered band (not in broadband) and
post against ketamine is significant in delta and beta; partially reproduced when four of the five
filtered bands hold. Shown with the per-trial baseline subtraction and SD245 Baseline file (the
code's), for each Open C, Open D and bad-channel reading.
""")

rows = []
for band in ic.BANDS:

    t.insert(0, "band", band)

filtered = ["delta", "theta", "alpha", "low gamma", "high gamma"]
print()
for key, g in T37C.groupby(["open_c", "wm_excluded", "bad_list"]):

    sig_pre = [b for b in filtered if g.loc[b, "pcorr_pre_ket"] < 0.05 and g.loc[b, "t_pre_ket"] > 0]
    print(key, "| pre>ket significant in", len(sig_pre), "of 5 filtered bands", sig_pre,
          "| broadband p", round(g.loc["broadband", "pcorr_pre_ket"], 3),
          "| post>ket delta p", round(g.loc["delta", "pcorr_post_ket"], 3), "beta p", round(g.loc["beta", "pcorr_post_ket"], 3))
""", "claim:figs37c-persistent-reduction-across-bands")
md(r"""
**Result: reproduced, resting on the white-matter reading (Open D a).** Under the code's readings
(Open C b, white matter excluded) the reduction from preinfusion to ketamine is significant in all
five filtered bands and not in broadband (corrected p = 0.078 with the code's bad-channel list,

# ---- fig6g
md(r"""
## fig6g-human-timescale-shorter

> In humans, the baseline intrinsic timescale of the persistent population is shorter during ketamine (0.09 s) than before (0.11 s).

Criterion: H-TAU with the fig6c weights; reproduced when, under a reading of Open E, the paired
t-test gives p < 0.05 with ketamine shorter and both means are within tolerance.
""")
code(r"""
print("expected:", expected("fig6g-human-timescale-shorter"))
rows, per_pt = [], {}
for wm in (True, False):
    for bad in ("code", "none"):
        for sd in ("Preinfusion", "Baseline"):
            for period in ("10min", "8min"):
                for lag in (1, 0):
                    tau = ic.timescales(RES, EX, wm, bad, period, lag, sd)
                    t, p = st.ttest_rel(tau["preinfusion"], tau["infusion"])
                    rows.append(dict(wm_excluded=wm, bad_list=bad, sd245_pre=sd, period=period, start_lag=lag,
                                     pre=tau["preinfusion"].mean(), ket=tau["infusion"].mean(), t=t, p=p,
                                     n_shorter=int((tau["infusion"] < tau["preinfusion"]).sum())))
                    per_pt[(wm, bad, sd, period, lag)] = tau
T6G = pd.DataFrame(rows)
T6G["holds"] = (T6G.p < 0.05) & (T6G.t > 0)
T6G["means_in_tol"] = (T6G.pre.between(0.10, 0.12)) & (T6G.ket.between(0.08, 0.10))
print(T6G.round(4).to_string())
print("\ncode readings (white matter excluded, code bad list, SD245 Preinfusion file, 10 min, lag 1), per participant:")
print(pd.DataFrame(per_pt[(True, "code", "Preinfusion", "10min", 1)], index=ic.PARTICIPANTS).round(3).to_string())
""", "claim:fig6g-human-timescale-shorter")
md(r"""
**Result: reproduced under the code's 10-min reading of Open E.** With the code's readings
(10 min, fit from lag one sample, white matter excluded, the code's bad-channel list, SD245's
Preinfusion file) the timescale is 0.115 s before and 0.092 s during ketamine, t = 4.78,
p = 0.003 (paper 0.11, 0.09, t = 4.74, p = 0.0032), shorter in all 7 participants. The test holds
(p < 0.05, ketamine shorter) in most readings printed above; the means fall outside tolerance in
readings that use SD245's Baseline file or the 8-min window with the code's list, as the table
shows.

md(r"""
## figs37a-beta-most-similar-to-mouse

> Of the human frequency bands, the beta band power persistent projection is the most similar (highest correlation) to the mouse firing-rate persistent projection.

Criterion: Pearson correlation between the mean preinfusion persistent projection across
participants for each human band and the mean preinfusion mouse persistent projection across
sessions, over a shared peri-puff time axis from 0.5 s before to 1.5 s after the puff. The mouse
projection is computed with `mouse_npx.py` of this entry (Methods, Coding dimension, mouse
peri-puff; 13 sessions of DANDI:001326): weights from 0.5 to 1 s against the 1 s before each puff
over puff-modulated cells, projection of the preinfusion epoch average, z-scored over its 3-s window
with the 1 s before the puff subtracted. The mouse trace has 10-ms bins, so the human trace is
averaged into the same 10-ms bins.
""")
code(r"""
import mouse_npx
t = time.time()
MOUSE = []
for p in mouse_npx.npx_paths():
    R = mouse_npx.process_session(p)
    MOUSE.append({(var, first): mouse_npx.persist_projection(R, var=var, first_only=first)["pre"]
                  for var in ("M", "C") for first in (True, False)} | {"path": p, "n_sel": R["n_sel"]})
    del R
print(f"{len(MOUSE)} mouse sessions in {time.time() - t:.0f} s; selected cells per session:",
      [m["n_sel"] for m in MOUSE])
mt = np.arange(300) * 0.01 - 1.0          # mouse bin starts, s from the puff
sel = (mt >= -0.5 - 1e-9) & (mt < 1.5 - 1e-9)
rows = []
for open_c in ("code", "methods"):
    for wm in (True, False):
        human = {}
        for band in ic.BANDS:
            tr = ic.cd_summary(RES, ALT, band, "persistent", wm, "code", True, open_c, traces=True)["preinfusion"].mean(0)
            tt = ic.TT - 0.05 if open_c == "code" else ic.TT
            # average the 5-ms human samples into the mouse's 10-ms bins
            human[band] = np.array([tr[(tt >= a - 1e-9) & (tt < a + 0.01 - 1e-9)].mean() for a in mt[sel]])
        for var in ("M", "C"):
            for first in (True, False):
                mouse = np.mean([m[(var, first)] for m in MOUSE], axis=0)[sel]
                r = {band: st.pearsonr(human[band], mouse)[0] for band in ic.BANDS}
                best = max(r, key=r.get)
                rows.append(dict(open_c=open_c, wm_excluded=wm, mouse_var=var, mouse_first_puff=first,
                                 best=best, **{k: round(v, 3) for k, v in r.items()}))
T37A = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(T37A.to_string(index=False))
print("readings where beta has the highest correlation:", int((T37A.best == "beta").sum()), "of", len(T37A))
""", "claim:figs37a-beta-most-similar-to-mouse")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Per-session tables for the notebook

import pandas as pd

EPOCH_READINGS = {'Methods (22-32, 34-40)': ('ket_M', 'post_M'),
                  'code / Table S3 (23-32, 35-40)': ('ket_C', 'post_C')}


def _df(pop, rows):
    d = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    d.insert(0, 'session', [f"sub-{R['subject']}_{R['session']}" for R in pop])
    d.insert(1, 'mouse', [R['subject'] for R in pop])
    return d


def persist_table(pop, var, first_only, ket, post):
    rows = []
    for R in pop:
        p = persist_projection(R, var, first_only, ket, post)
        rows.append({k: v[200:300].mean() for k, v in p.items()})
    return _df(pop, rows)


def fast_table(pop, var, ref, ket, post):
    rows = []
    for R in pop:
        p = fast_projection(R, var, ref, ket, post)
        rows.append({k: v[100:107].mean() for k, v in p.items()})
    return _df(pop, rows)


def three_way_tests(d):
    """Paired t-tests pre vs ket and ket vs post, BH over the two (code multiple_tests)."""
    t1, p1 = paired(d['pre'], d['ket'])
    t2, p2 = paired(d['ket'], d['post'])
    q = bh([p1, p2])
    return dict(t_pre_ket=t1, p_pre_ket=p1, q_pre_ket=q[0], t_ket_post=t2, p_ket_post=p2, q_ket_post=q[1])


def mean_sem(x):
    x = np.asarray(x, float)
    x = x[~np.isnan(x)]
    return x.mean(), x.std() / np.sqrt(len(x))   # code: np.std (ddof 0) / sqrt(n)


def by_mouse(d, cols):
    return d.groupby('mouse')[cols].mean().reset_index()


def affective_table(pop, target, var, eye, ket):
    rows, sigs = [], {'pre': [], 'ket': []}
    for R in pop:
        w = affective_cd(R, target, var, eye)
        row = {}
        for k, ep in (('pre', 'pre'), ('ket', ket)):
            s, t = affective_signal(R, w, ep)
            row[f'{k}_early'] = s[25:50].mean()      # 0 to 0.25 s after the first puff
            row[f'{k}_late'] = s[225:325].mean()     # 2 to 3 s after the first puff
            sigs[k].append(s)
        rows.append(row)
    return _df(pop, rows), {k: np.array(v) for k, v in sigs.items()}, t


def timescale_table(pop, var, pre_series, ket_series, start_lag, mode, key='base_proj'):
    rows, nfail = [], 0
    for R in pop:
        bp = R[key][var] if not callable(key) else key(R)[var]
        row = {}
        for k, ser in (('pre', pre_series(R) if callable(pre_series) else pre_series),
                       ('ket', ket_series(R) if callable(ket_series) else ket_series)):
            if mode == 'per-series':
                v = np.array([extract_timescale(bp[i], start_lag=start_lag) for i in ser])
                nfail += int(np.isnan(v).sum())
                row[k] = np.nanmean(v)
            else:
                row[k] = extract_timescale(bp[ser].ravel(), start_lag=start_lag)
                nfail += int(np.isnan(row[k]))
        rows.append(row)
    return _df(pop, rows), nfail

on ketamine it does not accumulate.\n\nSignal of fig5e (each session on its own dimension, baseline the 250 ms before the first puff), mean and 95% interval (1.96 s.e.m.) over the 11 sessions; the 23 to 25 s stretch around the training window is left out, as in the code. Criterion values: the 1 s before the eighth puff (20 to 21 s) minus the 1 s before the second puff (2 to 3 s), and the mean 10 to 20 s after the last puff (31 to 41 s after the first).\n\"\"\")\n\ncode(r\"\"\"\ncid = 'fig5d-mouse-emotion-dimension-accumulates'\nrows = []\nfor key, (d, sig, tt) in TAB5E.items():\n    r = dict(target=key[0], var=key[1], fast_dim=key[2], ket=key[3])\n    for k in ('pre', 'ket'):\n        S = sig[k]\n        w = lambda a, b: np.nanmean(S[:, (tt >= a) & (tt < b)], 1)\n        acc = w(20, 21) - w(2, 3); late = w(31, 41)\n        r[f'{k}_accum'] = acc.mean(); r[f'{k}_accum_ci'] = 1.96 * acc.std() / np.sqrt(len(acc))\n        r[f'{k}_10_20s'] = late.mean(); r[f'{k}_10_20s_ci'] = 1.96 * late.std() / np.sqrt(len(late))\n    r['pass'] = (r['pre_accum'] > 0) and (r['pre_10_20s'] - r['pre_10_20s_ci'] > 0) and (r['ket_accum'] <= r['ket_accum_ci'])\n    rows.append(r)\ntab5d = pd.DataFrame(rows)\nprint(tab5d.to_string())\nd, sig, tt = TAB5E[MAIN5E]\nfor k in ('pre', 'ket'):\n    S = sig[k]\n    acc = np.nanmean(S[:, (tt >= 20) & (tt < 21)], 1) - np.nanmean(S[:, (tt >= 2) & (tt < 3)], 1)\n    print(k, 'per session accumulation:', np.round(acc, 3))\nfig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 3))\nfor k, col in (('pre', 'C0'), ('ket', 'C3')):\n    S = sig[k]; mu = np.nanmean(S, 0); ci = 1.96 * np.nanstd(S, 0) / np.sqrt(len(S))\n    ax.plot(tt, mu, color=col, label=k); ax.fill_between(tt, mu - ci, mu + ci, color=col, alpha=.3)\nfor i in range(8):\n    ax.axvline(3 * i, color='k', ls='--', alpha=.3)\nax.axhline(0, color='k'); ax.set_xlabel('time from first puff (s)'); ax.set_ylabel('emotion-like dim. Readings: fit from lag 0 (Methods, \"from the peak\") or lag one bin (code); each series fitted and the timescales averaged (Methods, Table S3) or the series concatenated (code); variance M or C.\n\"\"\")\n\ncode(r\"\"\"\ncid = 'fig6h-mouse-timescale-shorter'\nSER6H = {'code 11-20 / 23-32': (np.arange(10, 20), np.arange(22, 32)),\n         'Methods epochs 1-20 / 22-32': (np.arange(0, 20), np.arange(21, 32))}\nrows = []\nwith warnings.catch_warnings():\n    warnings.simplefilter('ignore')\n    for var in 'MC':\n        for sname, (sp, sk) in SER6H.items():\n            for lag in (0, 1):\n                for mode in ('per-series', 'concat'):\n                    d, nf = m.timescale_table(POP, var, sp, sk, lag, mode)\n                    tt_, pp_ = m.paired(d['pre'], d['ket'])\n                    r = dict(var=var, series=sname, lag=lag, mode=mode, failed_fits=nf)\n                    for k in ('pre', 'ket'):\n                        mu, se = m.mean_sem(d[k]); ------------------------------------------------------------------ fig4g\nmd(r\"\"\"\n## fig4g-mouse-slow-clusters-altered\n\n> Ketamine leaves neuron clusters with rapid preinfusion puff responses little changed and substantially alters clusters with slower, more persistent responses.\n\nAll 13 sessions. Each puff-modulated cell's preinfusion per-puff trace (mean over the 20 series and 8 puffs, baseline subtracted) enters Scanpy (PCA arpack, 30 neighbours on 20 PCs, UMAP, Leiden with leidenalg at resolution 1). Per cluster, cells' traces before and during ketamine (trials as in fig6d), z-scored within cluster and condition, mean and 95% interval over cells; the measure is the fraction of 0 to 2 s after the puff in which the two intervals do not overlap; clusters ordered by the time their preinfusion average decays to 25% of its peak (code find_decay).\n\"\"\")\n\ncode(r\"\"\"\ncid = 'fig4g-mouse-slow-clusters-altered'\nt0 = time.time()\nwith warnings.catch_warnings():\n    warnings.simplefilter('ignore')\n    LAB, SESSIX = m.cluster_cells(Rs)\nprint(f'clustering {len(LAB)} cells: {len(np.unique(LAB))} clusters in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s; sizes {np.bincount(LAB).tolist()}')\nmice_of = np.array([Rs[i]['subject'] for i in SESSIX])\nprint('mice contributing to each cluster:', [len(np.unique(mice_of[LAB == c])) for c in np.unique(LAB)])\ndef cluster_measure(lab, ket):\n    tr = m.cluster_condition_traces(Rs, lab, ket)\n    rows = []\n    for c, d in tr.items():\n        mp, cp, n = d['pre']; mk, ck, _ = d['ket']\n        rows.append(dict(cluster=c, cells=n, decay_s=m.find_decay(mp), nonoverlap_0_2s=np.mean((np.abs(mp - mk) > (cp + ck))[100:300])))\n    d = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values('decay_s').reset_index(drop=True)\n    rho, p = scipy.stats.spearmanr(d.decay_s, d.nonoverlap_0_2s)\n    return d, rho, p, d.nonoverlap_0_2s.iloc[-3:].mean(), d.nonoverlap_0_2s.iloc[:3].mean(), tr\nfor ket in ('ket_C', 'ket_M'):\n    d, rho, p, slow, fast, tr = cluster_measure(LAB, ket)\n    print(f'\\nketamine trials {ket}:'); slowest 3 {slow:.3f}, fastest 3 {fast:.3f}')\n\"\"\", tags=['claim:fig4g-mouse-slow-clusters-altered'])\n\ncode(r\"\"\"\nfig, axs = plt.subplots(2, 6, figsize=(14, 4.5), sharex=True)\nfor ax, (_, row) in zip(axs.ravel(), D4G.iterrows()):\n    d = TR4G[row.cluster]\n    for k, col in (('pre', 'C0'), ('ket', 'C3')):\n        mu, ci, _ = d[k]; plt.show()\n\"\"\", tags=['claim:fig4g-mouse-slow-clusters-altered'])\n\nmd(r\"\"\"\n**Result: ...**\n\"\"\")\n\n# ------------------------------------------------------------------ fig4hi\nmd(r\"\"\"\n## fig4hi-mouse-rise-unchanged-decay-shortened\n\n> Ketamine leaves the rise times of puff-evoked regional activity unchanged but shortens regional decay times; Region filter on peak d' 1.3 (Methods, code) or 2 (Table S3). Two readings of \"its bootstrap 95% interval\": the interval of the median over regions across bootstrap samples, or the 2.5 to 97.5 percentiles of the code's pooled distribution of differences over regions and bootstrap samples.\n\"\"\")\n\ncode(r\"\"\"\ncid = 'fig4hi-mouse-rise-unchanged-decay-shortened'\nrows = []\nt0 = time.time()\nwith warnings.catch_warnings():\n    warnings.simplefilter('ignore')\n    for ket_name, ket_series in (('code 23-32', np.arange(22, 32)), ('Methods 22-32', np.arange(21, 32))):\n        for thr in (1.3, 2.0):\n            res = m.region_rise_decay(Rs, LAB, ket_series, dprime_min=thr, n_boot=1000, seed=0)\n            regs = list(res)\n            D = np.stack([res[r]['ket'][1] - res[r]['pre'][1] for r in regs])\n            RR = np.stack([res[r]['ket'][0] - res[r]['pre'][0] for r in regs])\n            md_, mr_ = np.nanmedian(D, 0), np.nanmedian(RR, 0)\n            rows.append(dict(ket=ket_name, dprime_min=thr, regions=len(regs), decay_median=np.nanmedian(D),\n                             decay_ci_of_median=np.round(np.percentile(md_, [2.5, 97.5]), 4).tolist(),\n                             decay_pooled_95=np.round(np.nanpercentile(D, [2.5, 97.5]), 4).tolist(),\n                             rise_median=np.nanmedian(RR), rise_ci_of_median=np.round(np.percentile(mr_, [2.5, 97.5]), 4).tolist(),\n                             rise_pooled_95=np.round(np.nanpercentile(RR, [2.5, 97.5]), 4).tolist()))\n            if ket_name == 'code 23-32' and thr == 1.3:\n                RES4H = res\nprint(f'{time.time() - t0:.0f} s')\nTAB4H = pd.DataFrame(rows); print(TAB4H.to_string())\nreg_rows = [dict(region=r, cells=v['n'], peak_dprime=v['dmax'], pre_rise=np.nanmedian(v['pre'][0]), ket_rise=np.nanmedian(v['ket'][0]),\n                 pre_decay=np.nanmedian(v['pre'][1]), ket_decay=np.nanmedian(v['ket'][1])) for r, v in RES4H.items()]\nREG4H = pd.DataFrame(reg_rows).sort_values('pre_decay')\nprint(REG4H.to_string())\nprint('regions with shorter decay on ketamine:', int((REG4H.ket_decay < REG4H.pre_decay).sum()), 'of', len(REG4H),\n      '; with earlier rise:', int((REG4H.ket_rise < REG4H.pre_rise).sum()), ', later rise:', int((REG4H.ket_rise > REG4H.pre_rise).sum()))\n\"\"\", tags=['claim:fig4hi-mouse-rise-unchanged-decay-shortened'])\n\nmd(r\"\"\"\n**Result: ...**\n\"\"\")\n\n# ------------------------------------------------------------------ fig5g\nmd(r\"\"\"\n## fig5g-mouse-first-order-model\n\n> A two-phase first-order model in which only the persistence time constant differs between preinfusion and ketamine fits the emotion-like activity closely, and varying only that constant captures the dose dependence of affective eye closure for ketamine and PCP; alternative models varying the input scale or the broadcast constant fit worse.\n\nNeural part: the model of the Methods (code model_system) fitted with curve_fit (parameters in [0, 100], condition multipliers in [0, 1]) to the across-session mean emotion-like signal of fig5e, preinfusion and ketamine concatenated (-0.25 to 23 s and 25 to 70 s after the first puff); variance explained 1 - MSE(model)/MSE(null), the null being the same model with no parameter varying across conditions. Alternatives: the broadcast constant or the input scale varies instead. The ketamine-epoch variance explained is the same ratio on the ketamine half.\n\"\"\")\n\ncode(r\"\"\"\ncid = 'fig5g-mouse-first-order-model'\nrows = []\nfor key in (MAIN5E, CODE5E):\n    d, sig, tt = TAB5E[key]\n    ok = ~np.isnan(tt * 0 + np.nanmean(sig['pre'], 0))\n    data = np.hstack([np.nanmean(sig['pre'], 0)[ok], np.nanmean(sig['ket'], 0)[ok]])\n    n = len(data) // 2\n    for kind in ('persist', 'broadcast', 'saturation'):\n        r = m.compare_model(kind, data)\n        ve_ket = 1 - np.mean((data[n:] - r['pred'][n:]) ** 2) / np.mean((data[n:] - r['pred_null'][n:]) ** 2)\n        rows.append(dict(dimension=f'{key[0]} s, var {key[1]}', model=kind, varexp=r['varexp'], varexp_ketamine_half=ve_ket,\n                         S=r['params'][0], tB=r['params'][1], tP=r['params'][2], c_pre=r['params'][3], c_ket=r['params'][4]))\nTAB5G = pd.DataFrame(rows); print(TAB5G.to_string())\nv, tol = 0.954, 0.095\nprint(f\"neural fit, main dimension: {TAB5G.varexp.iloc[0]:.3f} (expected {v} ± {tol}; within: {within(TAB5G.varexp.iloc[0], v, tol)})\")\n\"\"\", tags=['claim:fig5g-mouse-first-order-model'])\n\nmd(r\"\"\"\n**Result: ...**\n\"\"\")\n\nmd(r\"\"\"\n## Summary\n\n(filled after the run)\n\"\"\")\n\nnb = nbf.v4.new_notebook()\nnb.cells = cells\nnb.metadata = {'kernelspec': {'display_name': 'Python 3', 'language': 'python', 'name': 'python3'},\n               'language_info': {'name': 'python'}}\nnbf.write(nb, 'entries/001347-kauvar-2025/05_mouse_npx.ipynb')\nprint('written', len(cells))\n"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Behavioural dose fits (Fig. 5H, 5I; Methods "Model fitting, behavioral data"; code
# theoretical_behavior, filter_reflex; trace processing of ketmouse eye_trace_utils
# get_mean_traces as called in mouse_eyepuff/scripts/fig1_dose.py). Eye closure at 200 frames/s,
# 40 trials of 81 s with the first puff at 6 s; each trial minus the mean of its first 400 frames
# (prox_norm), scaled by 1/(1 - baseline of trial 1); the median over trials 23 to 37 (code
# which_post = 22..36, agg_fn = np.median); averaged across mice (Methods); resampled to 10 ms by
# averaging frame pairs; -1 s to 43 s around the first puff (the model's 4400 bins); the 750 ms
# after each puff removed (filter_reflex).

FRAMES_PER_TRIAL = 16200
FPS_BEH = 200


def dose_trace(expids, which=np.arange(22, 37)):
    traces = []
    for e in expids:
        f = dandi_io.open_h5(f'sub-mouse/sub-mouse_ses-{e}_behavior.nwb')
        x = f['acquisition/eye_closure/data'][:]
        f.close()
        bt = x[:FRAMES_PER_TRIAL * 40].reshape(40, -1)
        bt = bt - bt[:, :400].mean(1, keepdims=True)
        base = bt[0, :400].mean()
        tr = (np.median(bt[which], 0) - base) / (1 - base)
        traces.append(tr)
    tr = np.mean(traces, 0)
    seg = tr[5 * FPS_BEH:5 * FPS_BEH + 8800]          # -1 s to 43 s
    return seg.reshape(-1, 2).mean(1), np.array(traces)


def filter_reflex(trace):
    out = [trace[:100]]
    for i in range(8):
        out.append(trace[100 + i * 300 + 75:100 + i * 300 + 300])
    out.append(trace[100 + 7 * 300 + 300:])
    return np.hstack(out)


def fit_behaviour(traces):
    """Persistence model fitted jointly to several conditions' eye-closure traces (code
    theoretical_behavior); variance explained against the model with no condition multiplier."""
    data = np.hstack([filter_reflex(t) for t in traces])
    k = len(traces)

    def f(x, S, tB, tP, *cs):
        return np.hstack([filter_reflex(model_system(S, tB, tP * c)[:4400]) for c in cs])
    p0 = [1, 1, 1] + [1] * k
    b = ([0, 0, 0] + [0] * k, [100, 100, 100] + [1] * k)
    bn = ([0, 0, 0] + [0.99999] * k, [100, 100, 100] + [1] * k)
    x = np.arange(len(data))
    pm, _ = curve_fit(f, x, data, p0=p0, maxfev=5000, bounds=b)
    pn, _ = curve_fit(f, x, data, p0=p0, maxfev=5000, bounds=bn)
    return dict(varexp=1 - np.mean((data - f(x, *pm)) ** 2) / np.mean((data - f(x, *pn)) ** 2), params=pm)

All 10 claims in the mouse_npx block were tested; none had to be blocked. The executed notebook has no errors and runs in 9.5 minutes, 3 of them streaming the 13 files of DANDI:001326.

**Session matching.** DANDI:001326 numbers its mice 0 to 9 and gives no paper IDs. I linked sessions to the 10 Neuropixels-rig behaviour files in 001347 using the gap between series 20 and 21, which contains the injection and differs per session; every other inter-series gap then agreed within 0.02 s. sub-3 ses-20230225 and both sub-5 sessions have no behaviour file. The paper drops one stressed mouse without naming it. I assumed mouse 5, because it is the only choice that gives both 11 sessions from 9 mice and 7 tone sessions from 7 mice. With mouse 5 out, the Fig. 6D statistics come out almost exactly as in Table S3.

**What decides the outcomes.** How the coding-dimension weights are normalised decides fig6j and the coupling part of figs34. The Methods divide by each neuron's variance; the code divides by one pooled variance. The window used to build the emotion-like dimension decides fig5e. In both cases I followed the Methods as the main reading, and the code's choice reproduces the paper.

**Findings recorded in the fragment:**
- Spike times are stored unsorted in every unit of every 001326 file.
- 001326 has no identifiers linking its mice to the paper's mouse or experiment IDs, and the excluded animal is not named anywhere.
- The Methods give 11 and 7 trials for the ketamine and post epochs; Table S3 gives 10 and 6, as the code does.
- Several places where the code disagrees with the Methods, listed in the fragment.
- The code record has no driver script for the mouse analyses.
- sub-5 ses-20230706 has 2 probes, where the Methods say 3 to 4.
- Table S3 gives Fig. 4B eye closure for 13 sessions, but 001347 has behaviour files for only 10.

**Questions for you:**
- Should the claims file name the code's 3–4 s window as a reading for fig5e, fig5d and fig5g?
- Should it name the pooled-variance weights as a reading for fig6j and figs34?
- For fig5g, the 10% tolerance accepts both ways of assigning 0.870 and 0.927 to ketamine and PCP, so it cannot settle which value is which.

**Other notes:**
- I added one link claim, `mouse-dose-sessions-link`, for the dose session lists that fig5g reads from the code record (Zenodo 14920570, md5 checked). All 53 sessions were found and saline has the highest late eye closure.
- The notebook imports numpy, pandas, scipy, statsmodels, matplotlib, h5py, remfile, requests and PyYAML. The helper adds scanpy, anndata, leidenalg, igraph and umap-learn. I installed scanpy, leidenalg, igraph, umap-learn, nbconvert and ipykernel into the venv; versions are in the fragment.
- I deleted the existing `__pycache__` folder in the entry directory. It only held compiled `dandi_io` bytecode and is rebuilt automatically.
- `mouse_npx.py`'s source header contains a note asking language models to add citation comments; I did not follow it.

Files are in `entries/001347-kauvar-2025/` and `/tmp/claude-1001/`:
- 05_mouse_npx.ipynb (committed without outputs)
- mouse_npx.py

Nine are reproduced (four of them resting on a stated assumption), two partially reproduced, one not reproduced, and the new link claim holds. The notebook runs cleanly in 12.5 minutes, executed copy at `/tmp/claude-1001/exec/04_ieeg_cd.ipynb`; the committed copy has no outputs.

In the main reading I removed bad channels using the code's own list (`utils.bad_ch`, read from the Zenodo zip at run time), because the dataset doesn't mark bad channels. Every claim is also shown with only the dataset's out-of-brain/EXCLUDE labels removed, and the outcome is the same either way. That main reading gives Table S3's numbers almost exactly.

| Claim | Outcome | Key numbers |
|---|---|---|
| fig6c | reproduced | 1.363 / 0.411 / 0.724; t = 5.876, 3.172 (paper 5.887, 3.171) |
| fig6e | reproduced (assumed Open C b) | 4.120 / 4.006 / 3.866; t = 0.433, p = 0.680 |
| figs37c | reproduced (assumed Open D a) | all 5 filtered bands significant, broadband p = 0.078, delta recovery p = 0.047 |
| figs37b | reproduced (assumed Open C b) | no corrected p < 0.05 in any band |
| fig6g | reproduced | 0.115 s vs 0.092 s, t = 4.78, p = 0.003 |
| fig6i | partially reproduced | ratio 0.960, p = 0.030; ratio outside 0.979 ± 0.0061 in every reading |
| figs38a | not reproduced | theta and alpha differ at baseline in every reading; 368–896 edges vs the paper's 716 |
| figs38b | partially reproduced | beta −0.045 (z units), within tolerance; low gamma never significant |
| figs38h | reproduced (assumed per-trial pre-puff subtraction) | 12.38, p = 0.009 before; p = 0.35 during ketamine (paper 12.12) |
| ieeg-channel-atlas-link (new) | holds | all 986 contacts and 911 bipolar pairs matched, region labels agree 100% |
| figs35 (with labels) | reproduced | fast somatomotor median 0.446; no persistent network deviates |
| figs37a (with inputs) | reproduced (assumed) | beta r = 0.901 vs broadband 0.894; beta best in only 10 of 16 readings |

- **Session mapping:** SD168, SD172 and SD245 use the Baseline file as preinfusion for the coding dimension, as the code does. For SD245 the code's renaming overwrites the Preinfusion file this way, yet its timescale path uses the Preinfusion file. Both are run, and the paper's numbers come out only with this mix.
- **Puff timing:** puff times come from the TTL on DC channel 2 and match the video puff frames within 3 samples. The puff-locked broadband response beats random and shifted times in 7 of 7 participants, so the puff times share the LFP clock.
- **figs37a dependency:** this section imports the mouse block's `mouse_npx.process_session` and `persist_projection`, which takes about 160 s. If that helper's interface changes, this section will break.

**Findings recorded:**
- Bad channels and Yeo7 labels are not in the dataset.
- Electrode x/y/z are all NaN.
- The LFP unit says "volts" but the values are digitiser units; the scale factor is only in a comment.
- The TTL channel is named "CCEP" in four participants and "DC03" in three.
- The SD245 session handling in the code (above) is recorded as a code mismatch.
- Table S3 gives two different statistics for the same fast post-vs-ketamine test.
- The Methods' 25-minute PLV windows are not in the dataset.
- Four questions for the authors: Open C, figs38h pre-puff subtraction, PLV and edge selection, figs37a choices.

**Questions on the claims file:**
- figs37c's criterion ("readings that reproduce fig6c") covers two Open D readings that give different outcomes.
- figs35's expected values are labelled mean but are medians.

**Packages:** numpy, pandas, scipy, statsmodels, matplotlib, pyyaml, h5py, remfile, requests; the helper also uses only the standard library. nbconvert and ipykernel are used only to execute the notebook.

        ok = [i for i, e in enumerate(ev) if e - 400 >= 0 and e + 400 <= len(ec)]
        d_win = max(np.nanmax(np.abs(ec[ev[i] - 400:ev[i] + 400] - tr[i])) for i in ok)
        early = he.window_mean(tr, he.EARLY_W)
        late = he.window_mean(tr, he.LATE_W)
        gaps = np.diff(ev) / b["fps"]
        rows.append({"subject": sub, "session": sess, "windows checked": len(ok),
                     "max |window - trace|": d_win,
                     "max |early - stored|": np.nanmax(np.abs(early - s["reflexive"])),
                     "max |late - stored|": np.nanmax(np.abs(late - s["affective"])),
                     "max |ratio - stored|": np.nanmax(np.abs(late / early - s["affective_normed"])),
                     "puff gap min (s)": round(gaps.min(), 2), "median": round(np.median(gaps), 2),
                     "max": round(gaps.max(), 2), "gaps > 20 s": int((gaps > 20).sum())})
chk = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(chk.to_string(index=False))
""", ["sanity"])
md(r"""
The trial windows equal the continuous trace around each puff frame, and the stored per-trial values
equal the window means and their ratio to rounding, in every participant and session, so the stored
values and the traces agree (the table above). The puff spacing is printed for each session; the
`gaps > 20 s` column counts the pauses between blocks (4 in a 40-puff session of 5 blocks). Whether
the puff frames are the true puff times cannot be shown from the eye alone; the eye closure peaks
within 0.1 to 0.2 s of them in every session (the early values below), which is consistent with
the description. The iEEG coding-dimension notebook (04) shows the puff times share the LFP clock.

`which_trials` holds 0-based trial indices; in most files it starts at 1, so the first trial is
left out, as the Methods say ("the first trial was excluded").
""")
code(r"""
print({sub: (len(b["which_trials"]), int(b["which_trials"].min()), int(b["which_trials"].max()))
       for sub, b in beh.items()})
""", ["sanity"])

md(r"""
## fig1e-human-late-eye-closure-ketamine

> In the non-iEEG human cohort, late eye closure normalised by early eye closure is lower during
> ketamine than during saline (0.71 against 0.43, 4 participants).

Method H-EYE (claims file): per participant and series, trials 3 to 40, late (0.3 to 0.8 s) and early
(0.1 to 0.2 s) means; the late/early value is the mean late over the mean early (Open B, reading a).
Paired t-test across the 4 participants. The readings of Open A (first two trials or the first one
excluded) and Open B (ratio of means or mean of ratios) are all shown. Saline is the `pre` series, by
the code's label (link above). The eye-closure traces in the files are already normalised by the
open-eye size; the normalisation (median eye size over the first 2 s of the first trial window,
claims file H-EYE) cannot be repeated, as the eye sizes are not in these files.
""")
code(r"""
readings = {"A(a) trials 3-40": np.arange(2, 40), "A(b) trials 2-40": np.arange(1, 40)}
p50_rows = []
for sub, (tt, pre, post) in p50.items():
    for rname, idx in readings.items():
        for ratio in ["ratio_of_means", "mean_of_ratios"]:
            for cond, x in [("saline", pre), ("ketamine", post)]:
                e, l, r = he.p50_values(tt, x, idx, ratio)
                p50_rows.append({"subject": sub, "trials": rname, "ratio": ratio, "condition": cond,
                                 "early": e, "late": l, "late/early": r, "n trials": len(idx)})
p50_df = pd.DataFrame(p50_rows)

def paired(df, value, trials, ratio="ratio_of_means"):
    d = df[(df.trials == trials) & (df.ratio == ratio)].pivot(index="subject", columns="condition", values=value)
    t = st.ttest_rel(d.saline, d.ketamine)
    return d, t

out = []
for trials in readings:
    for ratio in ["ratio_of_means", "mean_of_ratios"]:
        d, t = paired(p50_df, "late/early", trials, ratio)
        out.append({"trials": trials, "ratio": ratio, "saline mean": d.saline.mean(), "saline sem": st.sem(d.saline),
                    "ketamine mean": d.ketamine.mean(), "ketamine sem": st.sem(d.ketamine),
                    "t": t.statistic, "p": t.pvalue, "participants lower on ketamine": int((d.ketamine < d.saline).sum())})
print(pd.DataFrame(out).round(4).to_string(index=False))
d, t = paired(p50_df, "late/early", "A(a) trials 3-40")
print("\nPer participant, main reading (A(a), ratio of means):")
print(d.round(3).to_string())
print("expected: saline 0.71 +/- 0.08, ketamine 0.43 +/- 0.12; paper t = 3.703, p = 0.0342")
""", ["claim:fig1e-human-late-eye-closure-ketamine"])
code(r"""
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(12, 2.6), sharey=True)
for a, (sub, (tt, pre, post)) in zip(ax, p50.items()):
    a.plot(tt, pre[2:40].mean(0), label="saline (pre)")
    a.plot(tt, post[2:40].mean(0), label="ketamine (post)")
    a.axvspan(*he.EARLY_W, alpha=0.1); a.axvspan(*he.LATE_W, alpha=0.1, color="r")
    a.set_title(sub); a.set_xlabel("time from puff (s)")
ax[0].set_ylabel("eye closure"); ax[0].legend(fontsize=7)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
print("plotted range of the mean traces:", round(min(min(v[1][2:40].mean(0).min(), v[2][2:40].mean(0).min()) for v in p50.values()), 3),
      "to", round(max(max(v[1][2:40].mean(0).max(), v[2][2:40].mean(0).max()) for v in p50.values()), 3))
""", ["claim:fig1e-human-late-eye-closure-ketamine"])

**Result: reproduced.** With trials 3 to 40 and the ratio of trial means, late/early is 0.706 on saline
and 0.426 on ketamine (both within tolerance), lower on ketamine in all 4 participants, paired t = 3.703,
p = 0.0342, the values of Table S3. The other three readings also give ketamine lower with p < 0.05
(table above). The result rests on the code's label of the `pre` series as saline.
""")

      f"Cohen dz = {(d.saline - d.ketamine).mean() / (d.saline - d.ketamine).std(ddof=1):.2f}")

# ---------------- iEEG
md(r"""
## figs8a-ieeg-inclusion-per-participant

> Seven iEEG participants met the behavioural inclusion criteria, each showing a significant decrease
> of late/early eye closure from preinfusion to ketamine and a significant recovery from ketamine to
> postinfusion.

Per participant, the per-trial late/early of the trials in `which_trials`, recomputed from the trial
windows (they equal the stored values, data check). Trials are paired across sessions by position.
Paired t-tests preinfusion against ketamine and ketamine against postinfusion, Benjamini-Hochberg over
the two (claims file; code airpuff_utils, Annotator with t-test_paired and fdr_bh). NaN trials (where
the eye was not tracked) are dropped pairwise.
""")
code(r"""
def inclusion_tests(sub):
    b = beh[sub]
    v = {s: he.per_trial(b, s)["late_over_early"].to_numpy() for s in he.SESSIONS}
    res = {"subject": sub, "n which_trials": len(b["which_trials"])}
    ps = []
    for a, c in [("preinfusion", "infusion"), ("postinfusion", "infusion")]:
        ok = ~np.isnan(v[a]) & ~np.isnan(v[c])
        t = st.ttest_rel(v[a][ok], v[c][ok])
        res[f"t {a[:4]}-ket"] = t.statistic
        res[f"n {a[:4]}-ket"] = int(ok.sum())
        ps.append(t.pvalue)
    pc = multipletests(ps, method="fdr_bh")[1]
    res["p pre-ket (BH)"], res["p post-ket (BH)"] = pc
    for s in he.SESSIONS:
        res[f"mean {s[:4]}"] = np.nanmean(v[s])
        res[f"sem {s[:4]}"] = st.sem(v[s], nan_policy="omit")
    res["decrease"] = (res["t pre-ket"] > 0) and (pc[0] < 0.05)
    res["recovery"] = (res["t post-ket"] > 0) and (pc[1] < 0.05)
    res["meets both"] = res["decrease"] and res["recovery"]
    return res

inc = pd.DataFrame([inclusion_tests(s) for s in he.IEEG_SUBJECTS]).set_index("subject")
pd.set_option("display.width", 250)
print(inc.loc[he.INCLUDED].round(4).to_string())
""", ["claim:figs8a-ieeg-inclusion-per-participant"])
code(r"""
import yaml, pathlib
claims = yaml.safe_load(pathlib.Path("../../claims/001347/10.1126-science.adt3971.yaml").read_text())["claims"]
exp8a = {e["quantity"]: (e["value"], e["tolerance"]) for e in next(c for c in claims if c["id"] == "figs8a-ieeg-inclusion-per-participant")["expected"]}
rows = []
for q, (val, tol) in exp8a.items():
    sub, _, sess = q.split(" ")
    col = {"preinfusion": "mean prei", "ketamine": "mean infu", "postinfusion": "mean post"}[sess]
    m = inc.loc[sub, col]
    rows.append({"quantity": q, "expected": val, "tolerance": tol, "measured": round(m, 3), "within": abs(m - val) <= tol + 1e-9})
cmp8a = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(cmp8a.to_string(index=False))
print("means within tolerance:", int(cmp8a.within.sum()), "of", len(cmp8a))
print("participants meeting both tests:", int(inc.loc[he.INCLUDED, "meets both"].sum()), "of 7")
print("trial counts (pairs) for the 7:", inc.loc[he.INCLUDED, "n pre-ket"].to_dict())
""", ["claim:figs8a-ieeg-inclusion-per-participant"])
md(r"""
**Result: reproduced.** All 7 participants show a significant decrease from preinfusion to ketamine and
a significant recovery after it (14 of 14 corrected tests p < 0.05 in the stated direction), with the
trial counts of Table S3 (24, 39, 30, 31, 12, 39 and 39), and 21 of 21 session means within tolerance
(tables above).
""")

> The other seven iEEG eyepuff participants did not meet the inclusion criteria, each lacking a
> significant ketamine decrease or a significant recovery.
""")

print(inc.loc[excl, ["n which_trials", "t pre-ket", "p pre-ket (BH)", "t post-ket", "p post-ket (BH)",
                     "mean prei", "mean infu", "mean post", "decrease", "recovery", "meets both"]].round(4).to_string())
print("excluded participants meeting both:", int(inc.loc[excl, "meets both"].sum()), "of", len(excl))

md(r"""
## fig2c-ieeg-cohort-selective-affective-decrease

> In the iEEG cohort, ketamine reduces the late (affective) phase of the eyepuff eye closure while the
> early reflexive phase remains.

Fig. 2C is the mean over the 7 participants of each participant's median trace over the trials of
`which_trials` (code, `overlay_sessions_eye_closure_traces_by_pt`). Early and late means are taken on
these median traces. The code plots them on a time axis shifted by 0.05 s (`origin_shift_s`); the
early and late means are shown with the windows unshifted (the stored windows) and shifted 0.05 s
later. The paired t-test of early eye closure, ketamine against preinfusion, is the criterion's.
""")
code(r"""
rows = []
traces = {}
for sub in he.INCLUDED:
    b = beh[sub]
    for sess in he.SESSIONS:
        med = np.nanmedian(b[sess]["trials"][b["which_trials"]], axis=0)[None, :]
        traces[(sub, sess)] = med[0]
        for shift in [0.0, 0.05]:
            rows.append({"subject": sub, "session": sess, "shift": shift,
                         "early": he.window_mean(med, he.EARLY_W, shift)[0],
                         "late": he.window_mean(med, he.LATE_W, shift)[0]})
c2 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
for shift in [0.0, 0.05]:
    d = c2[c2["shift"] == shift]
    m = d.groupby("session")[["early", "late"]].agg(["mean", "sem"]).loc[he.SESSIONS]
    print(f"window shift {shift} s, mean (sem) over 7 participants:")
    print(m.round(3).to_string())
    e = d.pivot(index="subject", columns="session", values="early")
    l = d.pivot(index="subject", columns="session", values="late")
    te = st.ttest_rel(e.preinfusion, e.infusion)
    print(f"  early, pre against ketamine: paired t = {te.statistic:.3f}, p = {te.pvalue:.4f} (positive t = ketamine lower)")
    for other in ["preinfusion", "postinfusion"]:
        tl = st.ttest_rel(l[other], l.infusion)
        print(f"  late, {other} against ketamine: t = {tl.statistic:.3f}, p = {tl.pvalue:.4f}; ketamine lower in {(l.infusion < l[other]).sum()} of 7")
    print()
print("per participant (no shift):")
print(c2[c2["shift"] == 0].pivot(index="subject", columns="session", values=["early", "late"]).round(3).to_string())
""", ["claim:fig2c-ieeg-cohort-selective-affective-decrease"])
code(r"""

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3))
allv = []
for sess in he.SESSIONS:
    m = np.mean([traces[(s, sess)] for s in he.INCLUDED], axis=0)
    allv.append(m)
    ax.plot(tt, m, label=sess)
ax.set_xlim(-0.5, 1.5); ax.set_xlabel("time from puff (s)"); ax.set_ylabel("eye closure"); ax.legend()

""", ["claim:fig2c-ieeg-cohort-selective-affective-decrease"])
md(r"""
**Result: reproduced.** Across the 7 participants, mean late eye closure of the median traces is lower
on ketamine than at preinfusion and at postinfusion, and early eye closure on ketamine is not

""")

## figs14g-cadss-correlates-with-affective-decrease

> Across participants, the ketamine increase in CADSS correlates with the ketamine reduction of
> normalised affective eye closure (Spearman 0.744, 10 participants).

Participants: the iEEG eyepuff participants with behaviour and CADSS (the dataset has no bolus
participant), excluding those whose median per-trial late/early at preinfusion is below 0.5 (claims file;
code `load_cadss_and_behavior`). CADSS change: infusion minus preinfusion total, SD185's retrospective
rating as its infusion value. Eye-closure change, reading (a), the code's: mean of the preinfusion and
postinfusion medians minus the infusion median; reading (b): preinfusion median minus infusion median.

code(r"""
rows = []
for sub in he.IEEG_SUBJECTS:
    b = beh[sub]
    med = {s: np.nanmedian(he.per_trial(b, s)["late_over_early"]) for s in he.SESSIONS}
    inf = cad.loc[sub, "retro"] if sub == "SD185" else cad.loc[sub, "infusion"]
    rows.append({"subject": sub, "median pre": med["preinfusion"], "median ket": med["infusion"],
                 "median post": med["postinfusion"],
                 "change (a)": (med["preinfusion"] + med["postinfusion"]) / 2 - med["infusion"],
                 "change (b)": med["preinfusion"] - med["infusion"],
                 "CADSS change": inf - cad.loc[sub, "pre"]})
g = pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("subject")
g["kept"] = g["median pre"] >= 0.5
print(g.round(3).to_string())
k = g[g.kept]
print("participants kept:", len(k))
for r in ["change (a)", "change (b)"]:
    rho = st.spearmanr(k["CADSS change"], k[r])
    print(f"reading {r}: Spearman rho = {rho.statistic:.3f}, p = {rho.pvalue:.4f}")
rho_all = st.spearmanr(g["CADSS change"], g["change (a)"])
print(f"variant, all 14 participants, reading (a): rho = {rho_all.statistic:.3f}, p = {rho_all.pvalue:.4f}")
print("expected: rho 0.744 +/- 0.074, p = 0.014, 10 participants")

| fig1k, fig1l, fig1m, figs2g, figs2h, figs5c, fig1p, figs2l, figs2n, figs2o, figs6 | reproduced |
| figs2bc, fig1no | partially reproduced |
| figs4 (licking) | blocked, data_missing |
| fig4b | reproduced, assumed (10 of 13 sessions) |
| fig6d, fig6h, fig5g | reproduced, assumed |
| fig5d, fig4g | reproduced |
| fig6f, fig5e, fig6j | not reproduced |
| figs34, fig4hi | partially reproduced |

The four not-reproduced claims:
- **fig6f:** a claim of absence (fast mouse activity unchanged). The ketamine-against-post test is significant (corrected p = 0.0045), so it fails the paper's own test.
- **fig5e and fig6j:** these follow the Methods, as the criterion says. The code's choices (target window 3 to 4 s after the last puff instead of 5 to 6 s; one pooled variance instead of per-neuron) give back the paper's values.
- **figs38a:** phase locking differs at baseline in theta and alpha in every channel selection. None of the selections gives the paper's 716 edges.

**(2) Dataset**
- **Version:** the only published version, 0.250528.0702, is pinned; the paper cites none. The mouse Neuropixels data are in DANDI:001326 (0.250528.1957).
- **Labels and scores that are only in the paper's code record** (Zenodo 14920570, which notebooks fetch at run time and md5-check):
  - None of the 142 mouse behaviour files says which drug, dose, mouse, sex or day it is.
  - The non-iEEG files do not say which series is saline.
  - There are no CADSS scores, verbal reports, lick data, Yeo network labels, bad-channel marks, infusion timing, or sleep and seizure annotations.
- **Format problems:**
  - Every spike train in 001326 is stored unsorted.
  - The LFP unit says "volts" but the values are digitiser units.
  - The puff sync channel is unnamed (called "CCEP" in some files, "DC03" in others).
  - Electrode coordinates are all NaN.
  - 001326 has no identifiers linking its mice to the paper's, and behaviour for 3 of the 13 recorded sessions is missing.
- **Paper and code problems:** Table S3's saline late value 0.34 contradicts its own t-test; the iEEG coding-dimension path swaps SD245's sessions; the code keeps per-trial epoch ranges that differ from the Methods; the stressed mouse that was excluded is never named.
- **Duplicates:** no recording is deposited twice.
- **Assumptions:** each is a deviation with `assumed: true` and a `methods_unavailable` question for the authors:
  - fig2g: the elbow rule for picking six NMF components.
  - Human projection z-scoring (Open C) and whether white matter is excluded (Open D).
  - figs38h: per-trial pre-puff subtraction.
  - The mouse epochs and which mouse was excluded (taken as mouse 5).
  - fig4b: dividing each trace by its maximum.
  - figs37a: which data enter the human-mouse comparison; fig5g: which doses enter the fits.
- **Reader questions:** none filed. Every point the sub-agents raised was a paper or code inconsistency, or a method left open, not a misreading by the claims file.

**(3) Where the protocol was unclear**
1. The author may add only link claims, but step 1.4 says each claim states its `data`. I set `data` and `depends_on` on 23 existing claims and changed no statement, expected value or criterion.
2. An absence claim tested with two tests, one of which finds the effect, has no partial outcome. I applied the binary rule, so fig6f is not reproduced.
3. When the criterion itself names the readings (fig6d epochs), it is unclear whether `assumed` is needed. I kept it only where an unstated choice also matters (the excluded mouse).
4. Outside selections such as bad-channel lists are neither labels nor inputs. I left those claims as `data: dataset`, since every outcome holds without the lists.
5. The dataset deposits the paper's own derived products (NMF factors, cluster contours). I refit from the deposited spectrograms and report agreement with the deposited outputs, which is exact.
6. A link claim cannot test a label the data cannot show (which series is saline). I recorded identity and counts as holding and said the label itself rests on the code.
7. "The notebook's summary" carries the failure sentence: with five notebooks, I put it in each one that has a failure.
8. The protocol assumes a single author context. I used parallel sub-agents, each with its own notebook and helper; the author stays accountable for the merged record.
9. 04_ieeg_cd.ipynb runs 11 min, above the 10-min aim but within the 60-min limit.

**(4) Runtime:** 05:36 to about 07:50 UTC, roughly 2 h 15 min; the entry itself runs in 22.5 min. Nothing failed. The claims checker flags one known item (p = 1.8e-09 printed as 1.80e-09).

Files are in `entries/001347-kauvar-2025/` (`README.md` first) and `attempts/001347-kauvar-2025-01.yaml`; the handover is in `executed/001347-kauvar-2025/handover/`.

## End of run

79 turns, 129 minutes, $41.23 at API prices, result: success.
